niche.diet: Herbivore: soft leaf tissue of nieblon, paja_dulce, and musgo_faro.

links: Dense air (1.6 bar, D8) increases drag and lift at small scales.
High metabolic turnover requires efficient aerial dispersal between food patches.
Dawn cooling (D9) increases air density further, boosting wing loading and flight stability.

skill.effect: The creature glides smoothly across the ground, its micro-wings beating in a steady rhythm. You can guide it to travel a moderate distance while remaining completely unheard in the mist.

chains.weakness: Stamina drains fast in dry midday air.

journal.en: They don't fly; they sail the thick dawn.

plausibility.summary: Reframe as crepuscular **wing-assisted jumping + Drift Glide** (F4): 1–3 s of high-frequency beat to clear the litter layer, then expose large micro-wings and ride dawn ground fog / weak updrafts for ≤30 m. Midday weakness stays (lower humidity, thermals, higher evaporative cost). Do not claim dense air makes flapping ‘efficient’—claim it makes **gliding distance per beat** favourable. Optionally note six leg-pairs as reduced wings + walking legs (hexapod baseline, D30 empty herbivore-insect niche).

analogues.organism: Thrips and chalcid wasps use clap-and-fling at high wingbeat frequency; aphids and spiders use wind-assisted ‘ballooning’ between plants; ant queens and many beetles make short dispersal hops rather than continuous flight (Ellington’s insect flight framework).

chains.trait: Broad-spectrum compound eyes track dim movement.
links: Morning fog scatters yellow-white sunlight (F17, F8).
Dense air dampens high-frequency sounds, shifting communication to visuals.
Low-light conditions select for rhodopsin-rich retinas and reduced photoreceptor density.

skill.effect: Its compound eyes pierce through the mist, strongly tracking faint movements that would otherwise remain hidden. You can clearly spot nearby prey and approaching threats through the heavy fog.

chains.weakness: Blinded by direct sun glare or sudden flares (F10).
observe: Dilated in fog, pinched in bright sun

journal.en: Their eyes are wet lenses for the dim world.

plausibility.summary: Crepuscular activity (F3 26 h day, F8 ~180 foggy dawns) selects for motion vision in dim, scatter-dominated light (F17). For a skittish leaf grazer at swarm edge, compound eyes that pool signal in low light fit fog-trap ecology better than reliance on high calls that attenuate in grass and fog (F4). Meadow/shore predators (acechalunas, alula) are silhouette threats at dawn—motion detection is adaptive. Sun glare and rare UV spikes from flares (F10) plus high-slope UV habit elsewhere on the island (F14) justify midday/blindness weakness without breaking island UV budget at sea level (F14 0.9× at coast).
fixes: Crepuscular activity (F3 26 h day, F8 ~180 foggy dawns) selects for motion vision in dim, scatter-dominated light (F17). For a skittish leaf grazer at swarm edge, compound eyes that pool signal in low light fit fog-trap ecology better than reliance on high calls that attenuate in grass and fog (F4). Meadow/shore predators (acechalunas, alula) are silhouette threats at dawn—motion detection is adaptive. Sun glare and rare UV spikes from flares (F10) plus high-slope UV habit elsewhere on the island (F14) justify midday/blindness weakness without breaking island UV budget at sea level (F14 0.9× at coast).

analogues.organism: Cockroach (Periplaneta) and nocturnal/crepuscular moth compound eyes for motion in dim light; mantid ommatidia for prey tracking at dusk.

links: High pO2 accelerates plant alkaloid production (F5, F25).
Concentrated feeding overwhelms plant chemical defenses via throughput.
Swarm saturation reduces individual predation risk via predator gape limits (D25).

skill.effect: The creature devours nearby foliage in a frenzy, swelling noticeably as it feeds. This sudden feast strongly attracts the attention of hunters from the surrounding area.

chains.weakness: Leaves a chewed trail that alerts ground carnivores.
observe: Hundreds converging on a single leaf

journal.en: One mouth is a pest; a hundred is a storm.

plausibility.summary: Chain: alkaloid spike ← synchronized wounding ← many mouths ← dawn fog cover ← F8/F16. Drop pO₂→alkaloid rate; keep F25 ‘honest red veins’ as post-damage warning and Albombrilla albino secret (avoid toxic patches). Cap swarm density per plant object for biomass; +5 mass is gameplay fudge unless individuals are much lighter (~50–100 mg) for true carpet swarms.

chains.trait: Woven egg sacs anchor to plant axils.
links: Dense air slows moisture diffusion, but egg membranes still desiccate without micro-forest cover.
Forest understory maintains stable humidity near stems (F28).
Anchoring prevents swarm dispersal during night convection storms (F8).

skill.effect: The creature weaves protective silk to anchor its eggs firmly to a branch. This woven shield strongly resists the pull of heavy winds.

chains.weakness: Stationary target for aerial predators like alula.
observe: Fine silk threads stitching leaf axils

journal.en: They tie their future to the green stem.

plausibility.summary: Root anchoring in **F19 storms + F8 convection**, with axils as micro-greenhouse (F18 meadow/forest edge). Silk Bind = modified salivary/tarsal protein (cite convergence, not unique spider silk). Game carcass ‘six legs’ matches insect hexapod; rename flavour text if ‘six arms’ means three pairs of walking legs only. +3 defense vs wind is honest; vs alula needs crypsis or hairy silk, not just glue.
fixes: Root anchoring in **F19 storms + F8 convection**, with axils as micro-greenhouse (F18 meadow/forest edge). Silk Bind = modified salivary/tarsal protein (cite convergence, not unique spider silk). Game carcass ‘six legs’ matches insect hexapod; rename flavour text if ‘six arms’ means three pairs of walking legs only. +3 defense vs wind is honest; vs alula needs crypsis or hairy silk, not just glue.

analogues.organism: Embioptera (webspinners) silk from foretarsi; gregarious sawfly larvae silk matrices; lacewing eggs on stalks (different tactic, same ‘anchor off substrate’ pressure).

relations.note: Dawn hunters stalk alfombrilla swarms on forest edges.
Omnivorous frugivores snatch swarming alfombrilla for protein.

changelog.what: removed rejected references and non-existent root facts (roots recovered from the derivation items cited in the links, else F27)

secrets: Collect all six legs from carcasses to unlock Silk Bind.
Find the albino variant: pure white swarm that avoids red-veined plants.
Watch a full dawn-to-dusk cycle from a high meadow viewpoint to see the swarm synchronize with fog density.
moments: At first light, the meadow edge shimmers as a low fog rolls in. The alfombrilla emerge from the leaf litter, not crawling but drifting on the damp air, a living carpet of green-grey wings settling onto the grass tips. When a shadow crosses the sun, they vanish into the dew in a single synchronized ripple, leaving only bent stems and silence.

journal.en: They don't graze; they tide in and out.
The forest floor breathes with them.
